Quick commercial take from Sales:
- We can offer a mutual 45–60 day notice window for convenience termination; 30 days is operationally tight for customer data export/transfer and capacity reallocation.
- For annual billing: propose auto-renew in 12-month increments but allow customer to opt-out with notice; prefer opt-out 60 days before renewal.
- If Acme is signing an initial committed term (e.g., reserved Dedicated capacity), we should preserve an early-exit recovery equal to the remaining committed monthly fees or a flat termination charge to protect capacity economics. For standard hosted pay-as-you-go customers, pro-rata refund is fine.

Suggested commercial compromise to propose to Acme: 60-day mutual notice for termination for convenience, auto-renew only at the end of each 12-month term with a 60-day opt-out window, and pre-committed capacity subject to an early termination charge equal to the greater of 3 months’ committed fees or remaining pro-rata charges.

Laura — can Legal provide a short, customer-friendly snippet we can send? If Acme pushes 30 days, what level of concession would you need?

Thanks,
Karthik

Thanks — below is Legal's recommended position and a short snippet you can pass to Acme. High level: aim for mutual 60 days; limit automatic rollovers to fixed, defined terms; keep termination-for-convenience available but protect committed-reserved capacity.

Redwood position (recommended):
- Notice: mutual 60 days prior written notice for termination for convenience.
- Auto-renew: Agreement renews automatically for successive 12‑month periods unless either party provides at least 60 days’ prior written notice of non‑renewal before the then‑current term expires.
- Termination for committed capacity: Customer may terminate for convenience but will be responsible for either (a) pro‑rated charges through the effective termination date, or (b) if termination occurs during an initial committed term, an early termination fee equal to the greater of three (3) months’ committed fees or the remaining pro‑rata fees for the committed term.

Client-facing snippet (copy/paste):
"Either party may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon sixty (60) days’ prior written notice. The Agreement shall automatically renew for successive twelve (12) month terms unless either party provides sixty (60) days’ prior written notice of non‑renewal. If Customer terminates during an initial committed term for Dedicated or Reserved capacity, Customer will be responsible for an early termination amount equal to the greater of (i) three (3) months’ committed fees or (ii) remaining pro‑rata fees for the committed period. For non‑committed, pay‑as‑you‑go Customers, Redwood will provide a pro‑rata refund for prepaid amounts through the effective termination date."

If Acme insists on 30 days, we can concede to a 30-day mutual notice only for standard hosted (non-committed) orders; keep reserved/dedicated on 60 days. That should close most procurement asks without exposing capacity risk.

Attachment: Redwood_MSA_termination_snippet.docx (contains the redline revision and tracked changes).

Laura Bennett

Elena / Tom — following up with a consolidated Redwood position so Procurement and Legal can route this back for signature: 

Summary of Redwood proposal (negotiated):
- Mutual 60‑day prior written notice for termination for convenience.
- Auto‑renew only in 12‑month increments; either party may opt out with at least 60 days' notice prior to the end of the then‑current term.
- If Acme signs reserved/dedicated capacity for an initial committed term, early termination will trigger the greater of (a) three months’ committed fees or (b) remaining pro‑rata fees for the committed period. For non‑committed (hosted) orders, Redwood will provide a pro‑rata refund for prepaid amounts through the effective termination date.

If Acme requires a 30‑day window for both hosted and reserved, we can accept 30 days only for standard hosted (pay‑as‑you‑go) agreements; reserved/dedicated capacity must remain at 60 days.
